newsitem.title: UK: Dehaene sees EMU starting on time in 1999.
newsitem.headline: Dehaene sees EMU starting on time in 1999.

text.p: Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene said on Tuesday he was convinced that the European Union's single currency would be launched on schedule on January 1, 1999.

Speaking to reporters after talks with British Prime Minister Tony Blair, Dehaene also expressed confidence France would agree by June 30 to the stability pact that will enforce budgetary discipline once the single currency has been established.
"I am convinced that the project will start on January 1, 1999," Dehaene told Reuters.

France's new socialist government threw a spanner in the works of the single currency on Monday by telling EU finance ministers it needed more time to consider the stability pact and discuss it with parliament.
"The important thing that was said yesterday was that everything would be settled by June 30," Dehaene said.

But Dehaene said it might be necessary to renegotiate how the EU should apply article 103 of the Maastricht treaty, which envisages coordination of members states' economic policies to balance the monetary rigour of the future European central bank.
He said this should be possible without even requiring a compromise between stability-minded Germany and growth-minded France.

"The stability pact clearly sets out how the criteria must be adhered to once the single currency has been launched. But already in the Maastricht treaty, the counterweight of that was article 103 on the coordination of social and economic policies.
"I think to reinforce that in another text would be no more than to provide the balance that Maastricht set down," Dehaene said.
